# Authentication

Use an existing, verified automation account in an active Twenty workspace. Give it the `ROLES` settings permission for role lookup and management. Role mutation guards also need visibility of current workspace members. Role deletion needs `APPLICATIONS` to inspect application defaults, or the global full-settings grant. Object-record permissions are separate.

Provision this account outside Terraform. Keep its membership and its current assigned roles outside Terraform-managed resources too. Maintain a separate recovery administrator with credentials the automation job does not use. The role resource cannot bootstrap accounts or manage assignments.

## Supply credentials

Prefer a secret-injection process that sets `TWENTY_EMAIL` and `TWENTY_PASSWORD` only for the Terraform process. Set `TWENTY_ENDPOINT` to the instance HTTPS base URL, or supply `endpoint` explicitly. Do not print credentials, place them in shell history, or commit them in Terraform files or variable files.

A sensitive attribute hides ordinary display output but does not keep its source out of saved plans. Terraform 1.10 or later supports sensitive ephemeral variables in provider configuration:

```terraform
variable "twenty_password" {
  type      = string
  sensitive = true
  ephemeral = true
}

provider "twenty" {
  endpoint = "https://twenty.example.com"
  email    = "automation@example.com"
  password = var.twenty_password
}
```

Inject `TF_VAR_twenty_password` at runtime, including when applying a saved plan. Do not use a persistent output or managed password resource as a substitute for an ephemeral input. Endpoint and email values may identify a private deployment, so keep actual deployment configuration out of this repository.

Explicit attributes override environment fallbacks. An empty explicit password fails rather than falling back to `TWENTY_PASSWORD`. Unknown credentials also fail. Password whitespace is preserved.

## Session behavior

The provider starts a new password session on each configuration, exchanges the login token for a workspace session, and checks the authenticated member and active workspace. Access and rotating refresh tokens remain in memory. They are not Terraform attributes, outputs, state values, or saved session files.

Requests and token renewal have bounded timeouts and honor cancellation. Renewal runs serially within a provider instance and replaces both tokens. If a session cannot be renewed, reconfigure the provider rather than supplying a token minted with server signing secrets.

Use HTTPS. Local HTTP requires `allow_insecure_http = true` and a `localhost` or literal loopback endpoint. This is only for disposable local testing. Redirects are rejected before credentials can be forwarded to another URL.

## Unsupported authentication flows

Password-disabled or SSO-only accounts, interactive MFA, CAPTCHA, and unverified email cannot complete unattended password login. The provider returns redacted errors rather than weakening server settings. Resolve account eligibility outside Terraform under your normal security policy.

API keys and userless client-credentials tokens do not support all planned membership operations in Twenty v2.44.0. The provider exposes password-session authentication only.

## Local acceptance tests

`make testacc` creates a disposable container stack, uses test-only automation and recovery accounts, and tears down only that stack. It removes ambient Twenty credentials and Terraform logging settings before running. Never point acceptance tests at a live deployment.

Ordinary unit, build, generation, and documentation checks need no account. Documentation commands remove Twenty credential environment variables and inspect schemas without logging in.
